name: CoinVello for WooCommerce
author: coinvello

sections.description:
CoinVello for WooCommerce adds a “Pay with crypto” option to your checkout. Customers are redirected to a hosted CoinVello payment page where they pay from any wallet (MetaMask, WalletConnect, or a plain QR code); your store is updated automatically when the payment confirms.

Non-custodial. CoinVello never holds your funds. Every payment is sent directly from the customer’s wallet to a wallet you control. There is no balance to withdraw and no counterparty risk.

No KYC or KYB to sign up. Create an account with an email address, generate an API key, and start accepting payments. Your customers never create an account or verify their identity to pay.

Features

  • Hosted checkout with locked exchange rate and configurable invoice expiry
  • Choose which assets to accept per chain (BTC, ETH, USDT on Tron, USDC on Polygon, SOL, and more) or accept everything enabled on your account
  • Clear admin notice when your CoinVello account runs out of processing credits
  • Real-time order updates via signed webhooks, with thank-you page polling and an hourly re-sync as fallbacks
  • Order notes with transaction hashes and block-explorer links
  • Underpayment tolerance: accept small shortfalls automatically, hold the rest for review
  • Overpayment and late-payment detection with clear order notes
  • Choose Processing or Completed as the status after payment
  • Test mode with separate test keys and secrets
  • Works with the classic checkout shortcode and the Checkout block
  • High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) compatible
  • Debug logging through WooCommerce > Status > Logs (API keys are redacted)

Refunds

Because CoinVello is non-custodial, refunds are not executed through the plugin. The order screen shows the payer details and links to the invoice in your CoinVello dashboard so you can send the refund from your wallet and then record a manual refund in WooCommerce.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.4+, WooCommerce 8.0+, PHP 8.1+
  • A CoinVello account (coinvello.com) with an API key and a webhook endpoint

Links

  • Developer documentation: coinvello.com/developers
  • API reference for AI assistants and agents: coinvello.com/llms-full.txt
  • Support: coinvello.com/contact

External services

This plugin connects to the CoinVello API (https://api.coinvello.com) to create checkout sessions, read invoice and payment status and list supported assets. The order amount, currency, order number, the customer’s email and name (for the payment receipt), the return URLs and your store name are sent when a customer chooses to pay with crypto; nothing is sent until then. CoinVello calls your store’s webhook URL to report payment events; every call is signed and verified before an order is touched. Customers are redirected to the hosted payment page at https://pay.coinvello.com. See the CoinVello terms of service and privacy policy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the coinvello-for-woocommerce folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install the zip from Plugins > Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Payments > CoinVello.
  4. Paste your test and/or live API key from the CoinVello dashboard (Developers > API keys).
  5. In the CoinVello dashboard, create a webhook endpoint pointing at the URL shown at the top of the settings page (https://your-store.example/?wc-api=coinvello), subscribe it to the invoice.* and payment.* events, and paste its signing secret into the matching “webhook secret” field.
  6. Pick the accepted assets, the order status after payment and the underpayment tolerance, then enable the gateway.
  7. Place a test order in test mode to confirm the full flow before switching to live.
sections.faq:
Does CoinVello hold my money?

No. Funds move from the payer’s wallet to yours on-chain. CoinVello detects the payment and tells your store about it.

Do my customers need a CoinVello account?

No. They pay from any wallet. No sign-up or identity verification is required to pay.

What happens if a customer underpays?

If the shortfall is within the tolerance you set, the order is marked paid with a note. Otherwise the order goes on hold with the amounts in the order note so you can resolve it with the customer.

What happens if a customer pays after the invoice expired?

CoinVello still reports the payment. The order is moved to paid status with a note asking you to verify stock before fulfilling.

Where are the logs?

Enable “Debug log” in the gateway settings and open WooCommerce > Status > Logs, source “coinvello”.

Can I use this with the Checkout block?

Yes. The plugin registers a payment method integration for the Cart and Checkout blocks.
